result.rationale: The finding claims admins can configure a path-restricted host that authorization then ignores. But the model's `before_validation` block explicitly strips paths: `self.host.sub!(//.*$/, '')`. So any path an admin enters is removed before save; the stored `host` column can never contain a path suffix, and `record_for_host` comparing hostname-only is consistent with what is stored. The premise 'even though the validator permits a path restriction' is contradicted by the diff: the validator may accept a path momentarily, but before_validation guarantees it is never persisted, so no path restrict

judged_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:10-19 — `record_for_host`/`host_allowed?` only compares the parsed URI's hostname (`uri.host`) against the stored `host` column, even though the model's format validator (line 2) permits admins to restrict a path suffix (e.g. `example.com/allowed-path`); any path/subpath restriction an admin configures is silently ignored at authorization time, so a Referer of `http://example.com/anything` is allowed even when the admin intended to scope it to `/allowed-path` .

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, any path suffix an admin enters is stripped before validation via `before_validation` (`self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), so the model does not actually support storing path-scoped allowlist entries. Additionally, `record_for_host` compares `uri.host` to the DB `host` column (`where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), so if a path *were* stored (e.g. via the migration’s raw SQL insert), it would *not* match and would deny rather than “silently allow any path”. The diff therefore doesn’t show an authorization bypass where `example.com/allowed-path` unintentionally permits `example.com/anything`.
